s_design.evidence_quote: Sixty extracted maxillary first molar teeth were divided into six groups (n = 10) according to pulpal inlay extension and marginal configuration.

no blinding of the single operator who performed all endodontic treatment, or of the two examiners who classified failure mode, is mentioned anywhere in the text

domains.evidence_quote: a two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was conducted to evaluate the overall statistical significance of differences
The authors declare no conflicts of interest.

citation.title: Mechanical behavior of endocrown vs. post-and-crown: a systematic review and meta-regression analysis
citation.authors: Fraga S, Balbinot GS, Quadros BG, Rodrigues SB, Foggi CC, Collares FM

s_design.anchor: systematic review with meta-regression of in-vitro studies (MATERIAL SR/MA row, 100)
s_design.evidence_quote: The eligibility criteria considered in vitro studies that evaluated the load-to-fracture of endodontically treated teeth restored with endocrowns and had a control group consisting of teeth restored with post-and-crown.

domains.note: no mention of PROSPERO or any pre-registered protocol anywhere in Methods or elsewhere in the full text; searched for 'protocol', 'PROSPERO', 'registered' — none found

domains.evidence_quote: A literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, EMBASE, and LILACS databases for studies published up to September 2025.

Database searching identified 862 records. After removing duplicates, 511 records were analyzed by title and abstract. Of these, 417 were excluded because they did not meet the inclusion criteria, and 94 were deemed eligible for full-text analysis.
domains.note: reports a PRISMA-style screening account with counts (511 screened, 417 excluded at title/abstract, 94 assessed full-text, 25 included) and explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, but does not individually list or reason the ~69 studies excluded at the full-text stage

domains.domain: risk of bias assessment of included studies
domains.evidence_quote: Two authors (S.F. and B.N.Q.) independently assessed the risk of bias in the included studies using the RoBDEMAT tool (14), evaluating four domains.
The model was adjusted for a Monte Carlo permutation test for meta-regression to consider possible overestimations in the model.

domains.note: no funnel plot, Egger's test, or any other publication-bias assessment is mentioned anywhere in Methods or Results; searched for 'publication bias', 'funnel', 'Egger' — none found
